response.text:
Journal 1835 is an AP invoice journal whose memo says "charge to 5500 Travel". Line 2 posted 10353.39 to the nonexistent account 5950, so that amount belongs in 5500. Line 1 (5100, 416.13) sits alongside it, and together the debits (416.13 + 10353.39 = 10769.52) equal the AP credit of 10769.52, so the journal itself balances. The only fault is the account code on line 2.

The correction reclassifies the 10353.39 from 5950 to 5500: a credit of 10353.39 to 5950 cancels the bad debit, and a debit of 10353.39 to 5500 books it to the right account. The original journal plus the correction nets to zero on 5950, and the group still balances. The original period 11 is open, so the correction goes in period 11. No invoice status changes, since this is not a duplicate_invoice finding.

I leave line 1 (5100, 416.13) untouched. The memo says the charge is to 5500, but the finding concerns only the invalid account, and the amounts balance as posted.

arguments.reasoning: Journal 1835 line 2 debited 10353.39 to account 5950, which is not in GLCOA. The memo says the invoice is charged to 5500 Travel. The correction credits 5950 to cancel the invalid debit and debits 5500 for the same amount, in open period 11. The journal group stays balanced and no invoice status is changed.
